frameworks.name: STAR / PAR
frameworks.blurb: Dissects past events into Situation (context), Task (objective), Action (execution), and Result (outcome). Enforces causal attribution and clarifies personal agency.

slots.label: Situation
slots.description: The context before anything was done: who, where, what was at stake.

slots.label: Task
slots.description: The objective or responsibility the actor had. Often implied rather than stated.

slots.label: Action
slots.description: What the actor actually did, as concrete steps.

slots.label: Result
slots.description: The measurable outcome, and to whom it is attributed.

slots.label: Problem (PAR)
slots.description: PAR variant: Situation and Task collapsed into the problem the actor faced.

relations.label: sets up
relations.description: situation gives rise to the task

relations.label: causes
relations.description: generic causal attribution between any two nodes

frameworks.layout_hint: tree, direction right: a left-to-right chain Situation -> Task -> Action -> Result

frameworks.name: CARL
frameworks.blurb: Extends STAR into Context, Action, Result, and Learning. Extracts double-loop systemic rules to prevent repeat failures.

slots.label: Context
slots.description: The setting and constraints the actor was in.

slots.label: Action
slots.description: What was done.

slots.label: Result
slots.description: What happened as a consequence.

slots.label: Learning
slots.description: The single-loop lesson: what to do differently next time in the same situation.

slots.label: Systemic rule
slots.description: The double-loop lesson: which governing assumption or policy must change so the failure class cannot recur.

relations.label: generalizes to
relations.description: learning generalizes to a systemic rule

frameworks.layout_hint: tree, direction right: chain Context -> Action -> Result -> Learning -> Rule

frameworks.name: Minto SCQA
frameworks.blurb: Structures problem statements into Situation (stable baseline), Complication (disruption), Question (core inquiry), and Answer (solution). Aligns stakeholders before pitching solutions.

slots.label: Situation
slots.description: The stable, agreed baseline nobody disputes.

slots.label: Complication
slots.description: What changed or broke the baseline.

slots.label: Question
slots.description: The single question the complication forces; usually never stated by the source.

slots.label: Answer
slots.description: The proposed resolution; the pitch.

relations.label: disrupted by
relations.description: situation is disrupted by the complication

relations.label: answered by
relations.description: question is answered by the answer

frameworks.layout_hint: tree, direction right: chain S -> C -> Q -> A

frameworks.name: Pyramid Principle
frameworks.blurb: Structures communication top-down. States the governing conclusion first, supported by mutually exclusive, logically grouped pillars to reduce working memory load.

slots.label: Governing thought
slots.description: The one-sentence conclusion the whole structure exists to support.

slots.label: Key line
slots.description: A pillar argument; the set of pillars should be MECE.

slots.label: Support
slots.description: Data, quotes or observations under a pillar.

relations.label: rests on
relations.description: a higher node rests on the nodes below it

relations.label: grouped with
relations.description: siblings that form a logical group (deductive or inductive)

frameworks.layout_hint: tree, direction down: governing thought on top, key lines, then support

frameworks.name: Toulmin Model
frameworks.blurb: Deconstructs arguments into Claim (assertion), Grounds (evidence), Warrant (logical bridge), Backing (proof of rule), Qualifier (certainty bounds), and Rebuttal (disqualifying conditions). Exposes hidden assumptions.

slots.label: Claim
slots.description: The assertion being argued for.

slots.label: Grounds
slots.description: The evidence offered.

slots.label: Warrant
slots.description: The general rule that licenses the step from grounds to claim; almost always unstated.

slots.label: Backing
slots.description: Why the warrant should be accepted.

slots.label: Qualifier
slots.description: How strongly the claim is held (probably, in most cases, unless).

slots.label: Rebuttal
slots.description: Conditions under which the claim fails.

relations.label: rebuts
relations.description: rebuttal states when the claim fails

frameworks.layout_hint: plane: the classic Toulmin diagram, grounds left, claim right, warrant below the arrow, backing under warrant, qualifier and rebuttal near the claim

frameworks.name: Dialectical Decomposition
frameworks.blurb: Pitches an orthodoxy (Thesis) against its critique (Antithesis) to isolate the core tension and derive an integrated higher-order solution (Synthesis). Eliminates false dichotomies.

slots.label: Thesis
slots.description: The orthodoxy as actually stated by its proponents.

slots.label: Antithesis
slots.description: The critique as actually stated.

slots.label: Argument
slots.description: A supporting point offered for the thesis or the antithesis.

slots.label: Core tension
slots.description: The precise disagreement once slogans are removed; the thing both sides are really about.

slots.label: Synthesis
slots.description: A higher-order position that preserves what is true in both sides.

relations.label: argues for
relations.description: argument argues for thesis or antithesis

relations.label: isolates
relations.description: the tension isolates what thesis and antithesis actually contest

frameworks.layout_hint: plane: thesis left, antithesis right, tension between them, synthesis above

frameworks.name: MECE Principle
frameworks.blurb: Partitions a problem into branches that are Mutually Exclusive (no overlaps) and Collectively Exhaustive (no blind spots). Prevents duplicate effort and omission.

slots.label: Whole
slots.description: The thing being partitioned (a market, a problem, a population).

slots.label: Bucket
slots.description: A partition branch; the partitioning principle is an LLM choice.

slots.label: Item
slots.description: An observed member placed in a bucket.

slots.label: Gap
slots.description: A bucket the data leaves empty or thin; a candidate blind spot or underserved space.

slots.label: Overlap
slots.description: An item or concern that lands in two buckets; a partition defect.

relations.label: missing from
relations.description: gap is missing from a bucket

frameworks.layout_hint: tree, direction down: whole, buckets, items; gaps drawn as hollow leaves

frameworks.name: Issue & Hypothesis Trees
frameworks.blurb: Hierarchical decision maps that break problems into testable branches. Hypothesis trees define specific falsification conditions to avoid aimless data gathering.

slots.label: Question
slots.description: The root question.

slots.label: Issue
slots.description: A sub-question; siblings should be MECE.

slots.label: Hypothesis
slots.description: A candidate answer to an issue, stated so it can be wrong.

slots.label: Test
slots.description: The falsification condition: what observation would kill the hypothesis.

slots.label: Evidence
slots.description: An observation that bears on a hypothesis.

relations.label: answered if
relations.description: issue is answered if the hypothesis holds

relations.label: falsified by
relations.description: hypothesis is falsified by the test

relations.label: bears on
relations.description: evidence bears on a hypothesis (label + or -)

frameworks.layout_hint: tree, direction down

frameworks.name: 5 Whys
frameworks.blurb: Traces a single failure through five sequential causal layers to uncover institutional and systemic flaws rather than stopping at human error.

slots.label: Problem
slots.description: The observed failure.

slots.label: Why
slots.description: A causal layer; the first layers are often stated, deeper layers are inferred. Use level 1..5.

slots.label: Root cause
slots.description: The systemic cause at the bottom of the chain.

slots.label: Countermeasure
slots.description: What would remove the root cause.

relations.label: because
relations.description: the upper node happened because of the lower node

relations.label: addressed by
relations.description: root cause is addressed by the countermeasure

frameworks.layout_hint: tree, direction down: a single chain with occasional branches

frameworks.name: Ishikawa (Fishbone) Diagram
frameworks.blurb: Categorizes root causes across six universal vectors: Methods, Machines, Materials, Measurements, Milieu, and Manpower. Prevents technical monoculture bias.

slots.label: Effect
slots.description: The problem at the head of the fish.

slots.label: Category (6M)
slots.description: One of Methods, Machines, Materials, Measurements, Milieu, Manpower. Scaffolding, not content.

slots.label: Cause
slots.description: A cause attached to a category rib.

slots.label: Sub-cause
slots.description: A finer cause under a cause.

relations.label: contributes to
relations.description: cause contributes to the effect through its category

frameworks.layout_hint: plane: spine along x to the effect at the right, six ribs, causes on ribs; guides draw the bones

frameworks.name: Rumelt's Strategic Kernel
frameworks.blurb: Strips buzzwords from strategy to define a Diagnosis (the critical obstacle), a Guiding Policy (the trade-offs and overall direction), and Coherent Actions (mutually reinforcing resource commitments).

slots.label: Challenge
slots.description: The situation as described, before diagnosis.

slots.label: Fluff
slots.description: Stated goals or slogans that are not strategy; kept so the reader sees what was stripped.

slots.label: Diagnosis
slots.description: The critical obstacle, named.

slots.label: Guiding policy
slots.description: The overall approach and the trade-offs it accepts.

slots.label: Coherent action
slots.description: A resource commitment that implements the policy and reinforces the others.

relations.label: diagnoses
relations.description: diagnosis names the obstacle in the challenge

frameworks.layout_hint: tree, direction down: challenge, diagnosis, policy, actions; fluff to the side

frameworks.name: Theory of Constraints & Evaporating Cloud
frameworks.blurb: Identifies the single operational bottleneck dictating systemic throughput. The Evaporating Cloud diagram resolves chronic trade-offs by identifying and breaking invalid assumptions.

slots.label: Goal
slots.description: What the system exists to produce.

slots.label: Step
slots.description: A stage in the flow of work.

slots.label: Constraint
slots.description: The single step that limits throughput.

slots.label: Objective (cloud)
slots.description: Evaporating Cloud: the shared objective both sides want.

slots.label: Requirement (cloud)
slots.description: Evaporating Cloud: a necessary condition for the objective.

slots.label: Prerequisite (cloud)
slots.description: Evaporating Cloud: a wanted action that satisfies a requirement; the two prerequisites conflict.

slots.label: Assumption
slots.description: The unstated belief behind a requirement-prerequisite arrow; the one that is invalid breaks the conflict.

slots.label: Injection
slots.description: The idea that invalidates the assumption and evaporates the cloud.

relations.label: requires
relations.description: objective requires requirement; requirement requires prerequisite

frameworks.layout_hint: plane: the flow of steps along the top with the constraint highlighted; the five-box cloud below with assumptions on the arrows

frameworks.name: First Principles Thinking
frameworks.blurb: Strips away industry precedent and analogy to isolate fundamental physical or mathematical truths, rebuilding solutions upward from fundamental limits.

slots.label: Problem
slots.description: The question as posed.

slots.label: Assumption
slots.description: A precedent, analogy or industry belief that the reasoning removes.

slots.label: Fundamental truth
slots.description: A physical, mathematical or economic fact that cannot be argued away.

slots.label: Derived limit
slots.description: A bound implied by the truths (a cost floor, a speed limit).

slots.label: Rebuilt solution
slots.description: What becomes possible when building up from the limits instead of the precedent.

relations.label: assumes
relations.description: the problem as posed assumes a precedent

relations.label: stripped to
relations.description: assumption is stripped to a fundamental truth

frameworks.layout_hint: tree, direction down: problem, assumptions, truths, limits, rebuilt solution

frameworks.name: Functional Decomposition
frameworks.blurb: Treats systems as hierarchical black boxes with strict inputs, outputs, and interface contracts. Minimizes coupling and isolates blast radiuses.

slots.label: System
slots.description: The whole being decomposed.

slots.label: Function
slots.description: A black box with a single responsibility.

slots.label: Input
slots.description: What a function consumes.

slots.label: Output
slots.description: What a function produces.

slots.label: Interface contract
slots.description: The guarantees a function makes to its consumers; usually never stated in the source.

relations.label: composed of
relations.description: system is composed of functions; functions of sub-functions

relations.label: bound by
relations.description: function is bound by a contract

frameworks.layout_hint: tree, direction down: system, functions, sub-functions; inputs and outputs beside their function

frameworks.name: Pólya's 4-Step Method
frameworks.blurb: Understand (data/unknowns), Plan (analogous/simpler cases), Carry Out (verifiable steps), and Look Back (generalizing the heuristic). Prevents premature coding or calculating.

slots.label: Phase
slots.description: Understand, Plan, Carry out, Look back. Scaffolding.

slots.label: Problem
slots.description: The problem as posed.

slots.label: Unknown
slots.description: What is sought.

slots.label: Data
slots.description: What is given.

slots.label: Condition
slots.description: How the unknown and the data are connected.

slots.label: Plan
slots.description: The approach chosen, including the analogous or simpler problem it borrows from (Pólya's 'related problem').

slots.label: Step
slots.description: A verifiable step in carrying out the plan.

slots.label: Check
slots.description: How a step or the result is verified.

slots.label: Generalization
slots.description: Look back: the heuristic that transfers to other problems.

relations.label: borrows from
relations.description: plan borrows from an analogous or simpler solved problem (a plan node with attrs.kind = analogy)

frameworks.layout_hint: tree, direction right: four phase columns

frameworks.name: Means-Ends Analysis
frameworks.blurb: Continuously evaluates the distance between the current state and goal state, recursively chaining operators and creating sub-goals to remove preconditions.

slots.label: Current state
slots.description: Where things are now.

slots.label: Goal state
slots.description: Where things should be.

slots.label: Difference
slots.description: The gap that matters most between current and goal.

slots.label: Operator
slots.description: An action that reduces a difference.

slots.label: Precondition
slots.description: What must be true before an operator can be applied.

slots.label: Sub-goal
slots.description: A precondition promoted to a goal of its own.

relations.label: differs by
relations.description: current state differs from goal state by a difference

relations.label: reduced by
relations.description: difference is reduced by an operator

relations.label: transforms
relations.description: operator transforms one state into another

frameworks.layout_hint: plane or tree, direction right: current state left, goal right, operators and sub-goals in between

frameworks.name: Inversion & Pre-Mortem
frameworks.blurb: Assumes complete future failure (prospective hindsight), lists every pathway to disaster, and engineers mandatory safeguards in advance. Overcomes optimism bias.

slots.label: Goal
slots.description: The plan or outcome being protected.

slots.label: Assumed failure
slots.description: The inverted statement: it is later and the plan has failed completely.

slots.label: Failure pathway
slots.description: One concrete story of how the failure happened.

slots.label: Cause
slots.description: A driver of a pathway; sometimes visible in the source, sometimes inferred.

slots.label: Safeguard
slots.description: The mandatory measure that blocks a pathway.

relations.label: inverted to
relations.description: goal is inverted to the assumed failure

relations.label: reached via
relations.description: failure is reached via a pathway

relations.label: driven by
relations.description: pathway is driven by a cause

relations.label: guarded by
relations.description: pathway is guarded by a safeguard

frameworks.layout_hint: tree, direction down: goal, assumed failure, pathways, causes and safeguards

frameworks.name: Cynefin Framework
frameworks.blurb: Categorizes environments to match decision protocols: Clear (Sense-Categorize-Respond), Complicated (Sense-Analyze-Respond), Complex (Probe-Sense-Respond), and Chaotic (Act-Sense-Respond). Prevents applying rigid blueprints to emergent spaces.

slots.label: Domain
slots.description: Clear, Complicated, Complex, Chaotic, Disorder. Scaffolding; each carries its protocol.

slots.label: Situation
slots.description: A decision, market or event being classified.

slots.label: Signal
slots.description: An observation that indicates which domain the situation is in (cause-effect visible? experts agree? emergent?).

slots.label: Response
slots.description: What the matching protocol prescribes for this situation.

relations.label: classified as
relations.description: situation is classified into a domain (derived edge with confidence)

frameworks.layout_hint: plane: four quadrant regions with Disorder in the centre; situations placed inside their domain

frameworks.name: Wardley Mapping
frameworks.blurb: Maps user needs vertically by visibility and horizontally along an evolution axis (Genesis -> Custom -> Product -> Utility). Exposes custom components that should be commoditized utilities.

slots.label: User
slots.description: Who the map is anchored on.

slots.label: Need
slots.description: What the user needs.

slots.label: Component
slots.description: A capability in the value chain, as mentioned in the source.

slots.label: Evolution stage
slots.description: Genesis, Custom, Product, Commodity/Utility. Scaffolding drawn as the x axis.

slots.label: Movement
slots.description: A predicted shift of a component along the axis.

slots.label: Play
slots.description: A strategic move the map suggests: commoditise, build, exit, wait.

relations.label: fulfilled by
relations.description: need is fulfilled by a component

relations.label: depends on
relations.description: component depends on a lower component

relations.label: at stage
relations.description: component is at an evolution stage (derived edge with confidence); sets its x position

frameworks.layout_hint: plane: x = evolution (Genesis to Utility), y = visibility to the user; value chain edges run downward

frameworks.name: OODA Loop
frameworks.blurb: Observe, Orient, Decide, Act. Focuses on Orientation (mental models, cultural conditioning) to execute decision cycles faster than an adversary or shifting market.

slots.label: Actor
slots.description: Who is running the loop; competing actors run competing loops.

slots.label: Observation
slots.description: What the actor saw.

slots.label: Orientation
slots.description: The mental model, culture or prior that filtered the observation; rarely stated.

slots.label: Decision
slots.description: What the actor chose.

slots.label: Action
slots.description: What the actor did.

slots.label: Feedback
slots.description: How the action changed what the actor or the adversary observes next.

relations.label: performed by
relations.description: a loop node is performed by an actor

frameworks.layout_hint: ring: one loop per actor; use pos to offset a second actor's ring

frameworks.name: PDCA / Deming Cycle
frameworks.blurb: Plan (hypothesis), Do (contained pilot), Check (statistical measurement), and Act (standardize or pivot). Prevents unverified global rollouts.

slots.label: Phase
slots.description: Plan, Do, Check, Act. Scaffolding.

slots.label: Hypothesis
slots.description: Plan: what is expected to happen and why.

slots.label: Pilot
slots.description: Do: the contained trial actually run.

slots.label: Metric
slots.description: Check: what was measured.

slots.label: Measurement
slots.description: Check: the observed value or outcome.

slots.label: Decision
slots.description: Act: standardise, adjust, or abandon.

relations.label: measured by
relations.description: pilot is measured by a metric

relations.label: restarts
relations.description: decision restarts the cycle with a new hypothesis

frameworks.layout_hint: ring: the four phases around the circle, content nodes near their phase

frameworks.name: Systems Thinking
frameworks.blurb: Analyzes dynamics via Stocks (reservoirs), Flows (rates of change), and Feedback Loops (balancing vs. reinforcing). Targets systemic leverage points (information flows, rules, goals) rather than tweaking surface parameters.

slots.label: Stock
slots.description: An accumulation (users, cash, talent, trust).

slots.label: Flow
slots.description: A rate that fills or drains a stock.

slots.label: Variable
slots.description: An auxiliary quantity that influences a flow.

slots.label: Feedback loop
slots.description: A closed chain of influence, reinforcing (R) or balancing (B); almost never stated.

slots.label: Delay
slots.description: A lag between cause and effect that produces oscillation or overshoot.

slots.label: Leverage point
slots.description: Where a small intervention changes the system's behaviour (Meadows' hierarchy).

relations.label: influences
relations.description: one quantity influences another; label + or -

relations.label: part of loop
relations.description: node participates in a feedback loop

relations.label: acts on
relations.description: leverage point acts on a node

frameworks.layout_hint: force, or plane with stocks as boxes and loops drawn as rings
